metadata.description: Knowledge graph served over the REST API (HTTPS + Bearer JWT via /auth/login): load a seeded KG, run the discovery queries against a known reference, stream NDJSON, negotiate CBOR vs JSON, and sustain concurrent READ clients.

notes: METRIC PROVENANCE (rmp #805): this baseline predates the storage.wal_bytes redefinition. Its storage.wal_bytes is the PRE-#805 quantity (an on-disk / snapshot WAL figure), not the durable write VOLUME that storage.wal_bytes names today (graphus_wal_bytes_written_total, a monotonic, reclamation-independent counter). On load, EvidenceReport::migrate_pre_wal_written_semantics relabels this value to storage.wal_retained_bytes and drops the amplification ratios (their numerator changed from store+retained to store+written), so the WAL-volume and amplification gates SKIP rather than compare two different quantities. To ARM those gates for this example, regenerate it once its runner reports graphus_wal_bytes_written_total as storage.wal_bytes (see examples/product-recommendations for the reference wiring).
storage.bytes_fsynced is a proxy: the WAL on-disk byte count (every committed WAL byte is fsynced before commit acknowledgement), not a directly-observed fsync counter.

storage.bytes_per_node / bytes_per_relationship are DERIVED: the measured durable store image (not the WAL, a transient redo log a checkpoint reclaims) amortised over the --nodes / --rels the example loaded into exactly that store. They amortise the WHOLE image (records + property blocks + token catalogs + free-list slack) over each element count, so they are not per-record sizes and do not sum to store_bytes — they are two views of the same image, and a deterministic, machine-independent footprint signal.

RESULT-SET VOLUME (rmp #717) — the REST response path, which this example exists to exercise, costs radically different amounts of SERVER memory by RESPONSE SHAPE at 150000 rows. STREAMING (NDJSON, or single-statement JSON with no Idempotency-Key) holds ~90 B of server RSS PER ROW (engine row materialisation only). The SAME query BUFFERED — a single-statement JSON the client made non-streamable simply by sending the API's own retry-safety Idempotency-Key header, or any multi-statement batch — holds ~2342 B/row (+335 MB peak), a 26x amplification: the serde_json intermediate tree the whole result is materialised into before a byte is flushed (rmp #383). The server's RSS per row was measured with proc_watch --watch over the server pid through each request. A production client that sends Idempotency-Key for safety silently loses streaming and pays that 26x — the fragility this example now surfaces.

RESULT-SET VOLUME cap — the buffered path is BOUNDED (MAX_BUFFERED_RESULT_BYTES = 16 MiB serialized, rmp #553/#475): a whole-node export (RETURN d, c, o) whose serialized size crosses the cap is REJECTED with HTTP 400 before commit, never OOM and never silently truncated. The cap gate FIRES in this run, so it is a real gate, not a green tick over an unreachable branch.

Throughput is the concurrency driver's HTTP requests over the window those requests were ACTUALLY ISSUED IN (concurrency_secs, measured by the python client) — it used to be divided by the whole server UPTIME, which silently understated req/s (rmp #699). The concurrency phase runs across 8 CLIENT PROCESSES (not just threads) because python's GIL makes a single-process driver saturate on itself and report a CLIENT ceiling as if it were the SERVER's — the exact scar tissue of social-network-large. Here the SERVER burned 7.415 cores while the CLIENT burned 6.12: the server out-worked the client, so this throughput is NOT client-bound. The per-request latency percentiles + payload sizes per encoding + NDJSON throughput are client-measured (GRAPHUS_STATS). Reads carry access_mode=READ so they engage the off-thread reader pool.

storage.* is the REAL on-disk footprint: the graphus.store image plus the graphus.wal DIRECTORY of segment files. The amplification ratios are those durable bytes over the generator's logical graph.cypher bytes — previously the denominator was an invented nodes*256 + rels*128 formula and write_amplification was left at a 0.0 placeholder (rmp #699).

Payload sizes per encoding (json_bytes, cbor_bytes, cbor_ratio) and the dataset size are DETERMINISTIC for a fixed seed+profile and are gated tightly; req/s, latency, CPU and RSS are machine-variant and are NOT gated (see kg_baseline_cmp).
Live measurement of graphus-server pid 1759864 over 6.000s uptime; CPU is the server's cumulative since-boot usage (the process is dedicated to this workload), RSS is sampled from the live process.
